preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(s) <= 10 for s in s_list) and all(1 <= len(t) <= 10 for t in t_list)
preconditions.description: Each string in the input sequences s and t has length between 1 and 10 (inclusive).

preconditions.expression: all(c.islower() for s in s_list for c in s) and all(c.islower() for t in t_list for c in t)
preconditions.description: All characters in the input sequences s and t are lowercase letters.
The sizes of the sequences s and t are between 1 and 20 (inclusive).
The number of queries q is between 1 and 2020 (inclusive).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= y <= 10**9 for y in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query year y is between 1 and 10^9 (inclusive).
The input sequences s and t have exactly n and m strings, respectively.

postconditions.expression: all(len(output_line) == len(s_list[(y-1) % n]) + len(t_list[(y-1) % m]) for y, output_line in zip(queries, stdout_lines, strict=True))
postconditions.description: For each query year y, the output line is the concatenation of s[(y-1) % n] and t[(y-1) % m], where s and t are the input sequences of strings.

postconditions.expression: all(output_line == s_list[(y-1) % n] + t_list[(y-1) % m] for y, output_line in zip(queries, stdout_lines, strict=True))
postconditions.description: The output for each query year y is the concatenation of the (y-1)-th cyclic index of s and the (y-1)-th cyclic index of t, where cyclic indexing wraps around using modulo arithmetic.
The number of output lines equals the number of queries q.
